plan.summary: Untrusted declared video evidence describes a Samsung Galaxy Tab S6 Lite that shows no display, audio, or host USB recognition, but exhibits possible charging/reboot cycles upon button combinations and has prior screen disassembly with a broken ribbon clip.

hypotheses.mechanism: Display assembly failure or disconnected display interface preventing image and backlight output while core board boots.
hypotheses.why: Unverified claims describe the unit dropping and restarting during button combos and drawing charging power without sound or picture, following prior screen replacement and a broken ribbon connector clip during disassembly.
hypotheses.safe_test: Connect the fully assembled tablet to a computer via USB while holding the key combination for recovery/download mode or observing device manager; qualitative detection of any USB device descriptor would favor a functioning mainboard with a severed display/backlight path over total board failure.

hypotheses.mechanism: USB-C sub-board, charging port, or data line discontinuity allowing power delivery negotiation or current flow but blocking USB host data enumeration.
hypotheses.why: The creator reported the device seems to take a charge or reboot on power input but fails to enumerate on a computer host, produce sound, or mount as a drive.
hypotheses.safe_test: Connect the device to an external display adapter (if supported) or alternate certified USB host ports under different external USB data orientations to observe if host enumeration occurs; appearance of host enumeration favors intact mainboard data lines over fractured port/data paths.

hypotheses.mechanism: Firmware bootloop, corrupted OS state, or PMIC power rail fault halting post-boot initialization before peripheral/USB driver bring-up.
hypotheses.why: Button reset sequences caused apparent drops and reboots without reaching an audible state or establishing a standard MTP/file transfer interface with the PC.
hypotheses.safe_test: Monitor external physical tactile heat distribution across the rear chassis and listen for subtle speaker pops or haptic feedback during a forced restart cycle; presence of transient localized warming or haptic vibration favors PMIC/processor activity entering a boot loop over an inert or disconnected power tree.

plan.next_safe_check: Inspect the device externally while connected to an external USB host/charger to observe qualitative host device manager enumeration responses and feel for external thermal changes across the chassis during a forced restart sequence; successful enumeration favors an isolated display/audio issue, whereas complete host absence with localized steady heat favors an early board-level or PMIC fault.
plan.uncertainty: All observations originate from declared, unverified video claims without genuine schematics, boardview files, or calibrated bench meter measurements; no baseline operating parameters are verified, making definitive fault isolation impossible without non-destructive qualitative probing.
